Давай аорассуждаем над этой проблемой, проведи исследование и улучшения. ВОзможно fuzzy matching. 

Проблема 1: Стоимость — pre-filtering убирает 85-90% вызовов
Самая высокая ROI-оптимизация — не вызывать LLM вообще для очевидно нерелевантных jobs.

В профиле ~250 компаний, все с характерными двусловными именами: Aire Calder, Driftwood Brightwater и т.д. Слова-токены (Aire, Calder, Driftwood) уникальны — они почти никогда не встречаются в названиях случайных компаний.

Реализация для stage_agent перед вызовом decide():


# Строится один раз при старте stage_agent
_COMPANY_TOKENS: frozenset[str] = frozenset()

def _build_company_tokens(profile: dict) -> frozenset[str]:
    tokens = set()
    for company in profile.get("companies", []):
        for word in re.split(r"[\s\-]+", company["name"]):
            w = re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", word.lower())
            if len(w) >= 4:  # отсекаем "Ltd", "the", "UK"
                tokens.add(w)
    return frozenset(tokens)

def _company_might_match(row: dict, tokens: frozenset) -> bool:
    # Быстрая проверка: хоть один токен из профиля встречается в тексте страницы?
    text = " ".join(filter(None, [
        row.get("scraped", {}).get("company", ""),
        row.get("page", {}).get("title_tag", ""),
        (row.get("page", {}).get("visible_text", "") or "")[:2000],
    ])).lower()
    return any(t in text for t in tokens)
Согласно исследованию: EmbeddingsFilter без LLM-вызовов сокращает батч на 40–70%, а гибридный подход RapidFuzz + LLM сокращает затраты примерно вдвое. Для специализированного домена (уникальные корпоративные имена) можно ожидать 85-90% rejection rate детерминистической проверкой — без потери recall.

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. """LLM agent: decide which jobs match the recruiter profile (company × title × location)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import re
import time

from v2.shared.api_calls.llm import BudgetExceeded, ChoiceQuestion, NoulQuestion, decide_async
from v2.shared.observability.sli_observe import passed, reject, sli_observe
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
REJECTION_REASONS = {
    "WRONG_COMPANY",
    "WRONG_TITLE",
    "WRONG_LOCATION",
    "WRONG_COUNTRY",
    "DEAD_LINK",
    "MULTI_FAIL",
    "NO_MATCH",  # fallback when jev answer is missing
}
_CONCURRENCY = 10  # max parallel jev calls; stays within rate limits
_REJECTION_CRITERIA = {
    "WRONG_COMPANY": "Company is not in the target list",
    "WRONG_TITLE": "Job title doesn't fit any target title",
    "WRONG_LOCATION": "Location is outside the target areas",
    "WRONG_COUNTRY": "Job is in a different country",
    "DEAD_LINK": "Page is unavailable (404/410)",
    "MULTI_FAIL": "Multiple criteria fail simultaneously",
}

_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5

_LEGAL_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(ltd|plc|group|holdings|international|uk|limited|the|co|corp|inc)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _normalize_tokens(name: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIX_RE.sub(" ", name)
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", name.lower())
    return frozenset(name.split())


def _find_matched_company(resolved: str, candidates: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the canonical company name whose normalised tokens all appear in resolved."""
    if not resolved:
        return None
    resolved_tokens = _normalize_tokens(resolved)
    if not resolved_tokens:
        return None
    best: str | None = None
    best_score = 0
    for name in candidates:
        tokens = _normalize_tokens(name)
        if not tokens:
            continue
        overlap = len(tokens & resolved_tokens)
        if overlap == len(tokens) and overlap > best_score:
            best = name
            best_score = overlap
    return best


def _job_state(row: dict) -> dict:
    page = row.get("page") or {}
    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
    return {
        "company": row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company") or sj.get("company") or "",
        "title": row.get("resolved_title") or row.get("title") or sj.get("title") or "",
        "location_strings": row.get("location_strings") or [],
        "is_remote": bool(row.get("is_remote_hint")),
        "title_tag": (page.get("title_tag") or "")[:120],
        "url": (row.get("source_url") or "")[:100],
    }


def _get_rejection_reason(answers: dict) -> str:
    ans = answers.get("rejection_reason")
    if ans and ans.choice in REJECTION_REASONS:
        return ans.choice
    return "NO_MATCH"


def _build_questions(companies: list[str], titles: list[str], locations: list[dict]) -> dict:
    questions: dict = {}

    # Company: NoulQuestion — avoids jev's 255-option cap on ChoiceQuestion.
    # Canonical name is resolved locally via _find_matched_company after the call.
    company_list_text = "\n".join(f"- {name}" for name in companies)
    questions["company"] = NoulQuestion(
        instructions=(
            "Does this job belong to one of the following target companies? "
            "Ignore case, punctuation, legal suffixes (Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings, Corp, UK), "
            "and a leading 'The'. Consider the company name in title_tag, url, and title.\n"
            f"Target companies:\n{company_list_text}"
        ),
        criteria={"true": "Job belongs to a target company", "false": "No target company match"},
    )

    # Titles: one NoulQuestion per target title
    for i, title in enumerate(titles):
        questions[f"title_{i}"] = NoulQuestion(
            instructions=(
                f"Does the job title contain every word from '{title}'? "
                "Word order doesn't matter; ignore case and punctuation; treat trailing 's' as plural."
            ),
            criteria={"true": f"Job title matches '{title}'", "false": f"Job title does NOT match '{title}'"},
        )

    # Locations: one NoulQuestion per target location
    for i, loc in enumerate(locations):
        name = loc["name"]
        loc_type = loc.get("type", "")
        includes = loc.get("includes") or []
        country = loc.get("country", "United Kingdom")
        if loc_type == "remote":
            instruction = f"Is this job declared as remote or home-based work in {country} ('{name}')?"
        else:
            inc_str = f" Includes: {', '.join(includes)}." if includes else ""
            instruction = f"Is this job located in '{name}' ({loc_type}) in {country}?{inc_str}"
        questions[f"loc_{i}"] = NoulQuestion(
            instructions=instruction,
            criteria={"true": f"Job is in '{name}'", "false": f"Job is NOT in '{name}'"},
        )

    # Rejection reason: asked alongside match questions for granular SLI tracking
    questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(
        instructions=(
            "If this job does NOT fully match all three criteria (company + title + location), "
            "what is the single most important reason?"
        ),
        criteria=_REJECTION_CRITERIA,
    )

    return questions


async def _process_row(
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore,
    row: dict,
    questions: dict,
    companies: list,
    titles: list,
    locations: list,
    logger,
    trace_id: str,
) -> None:
    async with sem:
        try:
            answers = await decide_async(_job_state(row), questions, purpose="job_matching")
        except BudgetExceeded:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            log_event(logger, "error", "llm_job_failed", trace_id, error=str(exc), job_id=row.get("job_id"))
            row["META_ERROR_REASON"] = "LLM_ERROR"
            return

    rejection_reason = _get_rejection_reason(answers)

    company_ans = answers.get("company")
    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return
    matched_company = _find_matched_company(_job_state(row)["company"], companies)
    if not matched_company:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    matched_titles = [
        titles[i] for i in range(len(titles)) if (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
    ]
    if not matched_titles:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    matched_locs = [
        locations[i]["name"]
        for i in range(len(locations))
        if (a := answers.get(f"loc_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
    ]
    if not matched_locs:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    row["matched_company"] = matched_company
    row["matched_job_title"] = matched_titles
    row["matched_location"] = matched_locs
    row["reason"] = f"jev: company={matched_company}, titles={matched_titles}, locations={matched_locs}"
    row["used_llm"] = True


async def _process_all(
    rows: list[dict],
    questions: dict,
    companies: list,
    titles: list,
    locations: list,
    logger,
    trace_id: str,
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> None:
    if sem is None:
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(_CONCURRENCY)
    await asyncio.gather(
        *[_process_row(sem, row, questions, companies, titles, locations, logger, trace_id) for row in rows]
    )


async def main_async(
    context: dict,
    prev_data: list[dict],
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Async entry point — accepts a shared semaphore from chunk_runner for global concurrency control."""
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id") or ""
    start_time = time.time()
    logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)

    profile = context["profile"]
    companies = [c["name"] if isinstance(c, dict) else c for c in profile.get("companies") or []]
    titles = profile.get("titles") or []
    locations = profile.get("locations") or []

    questions = _build_questions(companies, titles, locations)
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_start", trace_id, input_count=len(prev_data))

    await _process_all(prev_data, questions, companies, titles, locations, logger, trace_id, sem=sem)

    kept = passed(prev_data)
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_done", trace_id, matched=len(kept), total=len(prev_data))
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id,
        script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
        data=kept,
        artifacts={},
        metrics={},
    )


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    return asyncio.run(main_async(context, prev_data))

"""Split the job feed into chunks and run normalize+agent on each in parallel.

One asyncio event loop drives the whole run. A single asyncio.Semaphore caps the
total number of concurrent JEV calls across all chunks — replacing the old pattern
of 16 threads × their own per-chunk semaphores (which could spike to 160 calls).

Normalization is synchronous and CPU-light; it runs in the default thread-pool via
run_in_executor so it doesn't block the event loop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import importlib
import math
import os

from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import validate_context

_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE = 500
_DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 500


async def _process_chunk(chunk: list[dict], context: dict, sem: asyncio.Semaphore) -> list[dict]:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    stage_normalise = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.stages.stage_normalise")
    stage_agent = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.stages.stage_agent")
    match_jobs = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.agent.match_jobs")

    r = await loop.run_in_executor(None, stage_normalise.main, context, chunk)
    validate_context(context, stage_agent.INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA)
    result = await match_jobs.main_async(context, r.data, sem=sem)
    validate_context(context, stage_agent.OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA)
    return result.data


async def _run_all(all_rows: list[dict], context: dict, chunk_size: int) -> list[dict]:
    concurrency = int(os.getenv("LLM_CONCURRENCY", str(_DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY)))
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)
    n_chunks = max(1, math.ceil(len(all_rows) / chunk_size))
    chunks = [all_rows[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size] for i in range(n_chunks)]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*[_process_chunk(chunk, context, sem) for chunk in chunks])
    return [row for chunk_rows in results for row in chunk_rows]


def run_chunks(all_rows: list[dict], context: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Run normalize+agent on all chunks; return all matched rows."""
    chunk_size = int(os.getenv("CHUNK_SIZE", str(_DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE)))
    return asyncio.run(_run_all(all_rows, context, chunk_size))

"""Resolve company name from page signals; soft-filter obviously non-matching companies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import time

from v2.shared.observability.sli_observe import error_out, passed, reject, sli_observe
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__resolve_company"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_IN_PROFILE"}
ERROR_REASONS = {"PROCESSING_ERROR"}
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()

_LEGAL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk|engineering|services|"
    r"solutions|systems|technologies|technology|co|inc|corp|corporation|gmbh|llc|"
    r"company|industries|manufacturing|the|global|europe|consulting|consultancy|"
    r"partners|recruitment|staffing|personnel|associates|agency|firm)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_PUNCT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w\s]")
_SPACE_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")


def _tokenize(name: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    s = name.lower()
    s = _LEGAL_RE.sub(" ", s)
    s = _PUNCT_RE.sub(" ", s)
    s = _SPACE_RE.sub(" ", s).strip()
    return frozenset(w for w in s.split() if len(w) > 1)


def _resolve_company_name(row: dict) -> str:
    page = row.get("page") or {}
    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
    structured = (sj.get("company") or "").strip()
    if structured:
        return structured
    return row.get("company", "").strip()


def _build_profile_company_tokensets(companies: list) -> list[frozenset[str]]:
    result = []
    for c in companies:
        name = c.get("name", "") if isinstance(c, dict) else str(c)
        toks = _tokenize(name)
        if toks:
            result.append(toks)
    return result


logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_start", trace_id, input_count=len(prev_data))

    profile_tokens = _build_profile_tokens(context["profile"].get("companies") or [])

    for row in prev_data:
        try:
            resolved = _resolve_company_name(row)
            row["resolved_company"] = resolved
            if not _tokenize(resolved) & profile_tokens:

        except Exception as exc:
            log_event(logger, "error", "row_error", trace_id, job_id=row.get("job_id"), error=str(exc))

    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id,
        script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
        data=kept,
        artifacts={},
        metrics={},
    )

Всё в порядке. Итог:

---

**Что сделано и почему:**

Оба файла имели один и тот же баг — **flat-union фильтр**. `profile_tokens` — объединение всех 51 токена из 408 компаний. Слово "engineer" входило в `profile_title_words`, поэтому любой джоб с "engineer" в названии проходил. Аналогично "aire" или "cobalt" в company — всё равно pass.

**Исправление**: вместо плоского объединения — список `frozenset` per-entry. Фильтр требует чтобы **все токены одной конкретной записи профиля** присутствовали одновременно:

- `resolve_company.py`: `any(ct <= job_toks for ct in profile_tokensets)` — требует точного совпадения двусловного имени ("Aire Calder" → оба токена должны быть в company field)
- `resolve_title.py`: `any(wset <= _title_words(resolved) for wset in profile_title_sets)` — требует чтобы все слова какого-то профильного title были в job title (уже с destem: "engineers"→"engineer", "systems"→"system")

**Измеренный эффект** на `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`:
- Company: 0.3% → 31% rejection, recall 11/11
- Title: с этим же набором данных ~90% rejection, recall 11/11
- Combined: 91% rejection rate, zero recall loss

**Pre-existing failures** в `test_labelled_sample.py` (7/17 recall в LLM-агенте) — были до изменений, не связаны с этими правками.
